Piano Touch Lab is a toolbox, not a magi: Piano Touch Lab is a toolbox, not a magic wand. It provides the tools for measurement, analysis and calculation, but it is no substitute for the judgement of a trained technician.
Piano Touch Lab was born where two enthu: Piano Touch Lab was born where two enthusiasms meet: the piano and software. Curious to understand the mechanics of the instrument, I set out to explore the principles behind its geometry and its touch. That search led me to the work of David C. Stanwood, whose “Equation of Balance” and “New Touch Weight Metrology” shaped much of my thinking.

The static weight the level key exerts a: The static weight the level key exerts at the measuring point, tipped on its balance pin. Compared here against David C. Stanwood's standard curves.

The weight at the measuring point that b: The weight at the measuring point that balances 1 g placed at the capstan contact point: the leverage of the key alone.
The weight each spring takes off the mea: The weight each spring takes off the measuring point, placed above the back of its own key. Only the keys fitted with a spring carry a measurement.
The weight each wippen support spring ta: The weight each wippen support spring takes off the measuring point: the difference between the down weight without the spring and with it.
The weight of the hammer and its shank,: The weight of the hammer and its shank, pivoting without friction at its centre, shank horizontal, measured at the strike line radius. Compared against the 13 standard curves.
The weight of the hammer with the shank: The weight of the hammer with the shank removed.
The weight placed at the measuring point: The weight placed at the measuring point that brings the key into balance.
The weight to place at the measuring poi: The weight to place at the measuring point to balance 1 g of strike weight, through the shank, the wippen and the key.

The weight, to the nearest tenth of a gram, of the shank and hammer, pivoting without friction at the hammer centre, shank horizontal, measured at the strike line radius.
